questions.question: Which monumental 16th-century allegorical epic poem by Edmund Spenser celebrates Queen Elizabeth I as the Faerie Queene, Gloriana?
questions.explanation: Edmund Spenser composed The Faerie Queene to fashion a noble gentleman and celebrate Queen Elizabeth I.

questions.question: Who authored the foundational Elizabethan critical treatise 'An Apology for Poetry' (also known as 'The Defence of Poesy')?
questions.explanation: Sir Philip Sidney wrote An Apology for Poetry around 1580 to defend imaginative poetry against puritan attacks.

questions.question: Which University Wit established blank verse as the dominant majestic meter of English tragedy with 'Tamburlaine the Great'?
questions.explanation: Marlowe's mighty line transformed unrhymed iambic pentameter into the standard language of Elizabethan drama.

questions.question: What collective title is given to the educated late 16th-century dramatists from Oxford and Cambridge who preceded Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: The University Wits included Marlowe, Lyly, Greene, Peele, Lodge, Nashe, and Kyd, shaping Elizabethan theater.

questions.question: Which playwright pioneered the immensely popular Elizabethan revenge tragedy genre with his sensational work 'The Spanish Tragedy'?
questions.explanation: Thomas Kyd established the revenge tragedy conventions of murder, ghosts, feigned madness, and play-within-a-play.

questions.question: Which University Wit authored the popular prose romance 'Euphues: The Anatomy of Wit' (1578), spawning an elaborate courtly style?
questions.explanation: John Lyly popularized Euphuism, marked by balanced antitheses, alliteration, and rhetorical similes.

questions.question: Who wrote the tragic Renaissance drama 'Doctor Faustus', depicting a German scholar who barters his soul to Lucifer for 24 years of power?
questions.explanation: Christopher Marlowe composed Doctor Faustus around 1588 to 1592, exploring the limits of human ambition and knowledge.

questions.question: How many sonnets are included in William Shakespeare's definitive sonnet collection published by Thomas Thorpe in 1609?
questions.explanation: Thorpe's 1609 quarto contains 154 sonnets by Shakespeare, followed by the longer poem A Lover's Complaint.

questions.question: Which London acting troupe, originally called the Lord Chamberlain's Men, received royal patronage under King James I in 1603?
questions.explanation: Upon James I's accession, Shakespeare's acting company was awarded royal patronage as The King's Men.

questions.question: What was the name of the famous open-air circular playhouse erected in 1599 by Shakespeare's company on Bankside in Southwark?
questions.explanation: The Globe was built in 1599 using timber from The Theatre, serving as the chief venue for Shakespeare's masterpieces.

questions.question: Which Jacobean dramatist authored the macabre, poetic Italianate tragedies 'The White Devil' and 'The Duchess of Malfi'?
questions.explanation: John Webster achieved renown for his dark masterpieces probing corruption, court intrigue, and human dignity.

questions.question: Which playwright established the English 'Comedy of Humours' with his pathbreaking 1598 play 'Every Man in His Humour'?
questions.explanation: Ben Jonson based his comedy on the medical theory of four bodily humours governing human temperament.

questions.question: Which monumental English vernacular translation of the Bible was commissioned by the crown in 1604 and published in 1611?
questions.explanation: The King James Bible, or Authorized Version of 1611, profoundly enriched English literary prose and idiom.

questions.question: Who is celebrated as the 'Father of the English Essay' for publishing three expanding editions of pithy, worldly 'Essays' between 1597 and 1625?
questions.explanation: Francis Bacon adapted Montaigne's essay form into terse, aphoristic English meditations on civil life.

questions.question: Which brilliant poet-divine was the undisputed leader of the Metaphysical School of Poetry, celebrated for 'Songs and Sonnets'?
questions.explanation: John Donne revitalized English verse through passionate intellect, colloquial diction, and complex conceits.

questions.question: Which 18th-century critic first applied the term 'Metaphysical Poets' as a collective designation in his 'Life of Cowley'?
questions.explanation: Dr. Samuel Johnson coined the critical term in Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets in 1779.

questions.question: What is the defining poetic device of Metaphysical poetry, described by Dr. Johnson as heterogeneous ideas yoked by violence together?
questions.explanation: A metaphysical conceit is an elaborate, ingenious metaphor establishing unexpected parallels between disparate realms.

questions.question: Which Welsh-born Anglican clergyman authored the sacred metaphysical collection 'The Temple: Sacred Poems and Private Ejaculations' (1633)?
questions.explanation: George Herbert's The Temple contains intensely spiritual, beautifully structured devotional lyrics.

questions.question: What term is applied to the 17th-century courtier lyricists, loyal to King Charles I, who wrote polished verse on love, loyalty, and carpe diem?
questions.explanation: Cavalier poets like Herrick, Lovelace, Suckling, and Carew wrote elegant, carpe diem court poetry.

questions.question: Which Cavalier poet composed the celebrated carpe diem lyric 'To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time', beginning 'Gather ye rosebuds while ye may'?
questions.explanation: Robert Herrick's famous lyric urges youth to seize love and pleasure while youthful beauty endures.

questions.question: Which 1644 prose treatise by John Milton stands as a landmark philosophical defense of freedom of speech and the press?
options: The Tenure of Kings and Magistrates
questions.explanation: Areopagitica argues against the Licensing Order of 1643, defending unlicensed printing and free inquiry.

questions.question: What is the title of John Milton's supreme 1667 epic in unrhymed blank verse that aims to justify the ways of God to men?
questions.explanation: Paradise Lost narrates the rebellion of Satan, the war in Heaven, and the Fall of Adam and Eve.

questions.question: In which year did the Puritan-led English Parliament pass an ordinance ordering the complete closure of all public London theaters?
questions.explanation: Parliament closed the public theaters in September 1642 due to Puritan religious hostility and civil war.

questions.question: Which English king was tried for treason and publicly beheaded outside Whitehall Banqueting House in January 1649?
questions.explanation: The trial and execution of King Charles I in 1649 inaugurated the revolutionary English Republic.

questions.question: Who served as Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1653 until his death in 1658?
questions.explanation: Oliver Cromwell commanded the parliamentary New Model Army and governed Britain as Lord Protector.

questions.question: Which historic year marked the Restoration of King Charles II to the English throne, concluding the Renaissance literary period?
questions.explanation: The Restoration of 1660 reopened theaters and established the Neoclassical or Restoration literary era.

questions.question: Which 1579 pastoral work by Edmund Spenser, divided into twelve eclogues named for the months of the year, announced the new poetic renaissance?
questions.explanation: The Shepheardes Calender was published under the pseudonym Immerito and dedicated to Sir Philip Sidney.

questions.question: What is the title of Edmund Spenser's 89-sonnet sequence celebrating his courtship of his second wife, Elizabeth Boyle?
questions.explanation: Amoretti, meaning little love poems, records Spenser's joyful love, culminating in his Epithalamion.

questions.question: Which work by Sir Philip Sidney, composed around 1582, stands as the first sustained Elizabethan sonnet sequence in English?
questions.explanation: Astrophel and Stella charts Astrophel's star-lover passion for Stella, modeled on Lady Penelope Devereux.

questions.question: Which University Wit attacked William Shakespeare as an upstart Crow beautified with our feathers in his 1592 pamphlet 'Groats-worth of Wit'?
questions.explanation: Robert Greene's dying tract contains the earliest documented contemporary allusion to Shakespeare as a London playwright.

questions.question: Which massive history book, published in 1577 and expanded in 1587, served as Shakespeare's chief source for his English history plays and 'Macbeth'?
questions.explanation: Holinshed's Chronicles of England, Scotland, and Ireland supplied plots and historical data for Shakespeare.

questions.question: Which celebrated narrative poem by William Shakespeare, published in 1593 and dedicated to the Earl of Southampton, retells an Ovidian erotic myth?
questions.explanation: Venus and Adonis was Shakespeare's first printed literary publication, winning immense popular acclaim.

questions.question: Which satirical beast comedy by Ben Jonson features the cunning Venetian grandee Volpone and his scheming parasite Mosca?
questions.explanation: Volpone feigns mortal illness to dupe greedy legacy hunters Voltore, Corbaccio, and Corvino.

questions.question: Which acclaimed Jacobean comedy by Ben Jonson satirizes con artists Subtle and Face running a fraudulent laboratory during a London plague outbreak?
options: Every Man Out of His Humour
questions.explanation: The Alchemist ruthlessly mocks greed and gullibility through mock-scientific alchemy.

questions.question: Which intense Jacobean psychological tragedy by Thomas Middleton and William Rowley centers on Beatrice-Joanna and the deformed servant De Flores?
questions.explanation: The Changeling dramatises Beatrice-Joanna hiring De Flores to murder her suitor, becoming bound to her accomplice.

questions.question: In John Webster's 'The Duchess of Malfi', which cynical spy and malcontent is employed by the Duke and Cardinal to murder the virtuous Duchess?
questions.explanation: Bosola serves as spy and executioner, eventually seeking remorseful vengeance against his corrupt masters.

questions.question: Which famous metaphysical poem by Andrew Marvell urges his beloved to seize passion before the grave, opening 'Had we but world enough, and time'?
questions.explanation: Marvell's masterpiece uses vivid metaphysical imagery to urge immediate consumption of love against flying Time.

questions.question: Which Royalist Cavalier lyric by Richard Lovelace contains the immortal lines 'Stone walls do not a prison make, / Nor iron bars a cage'?
options: To Lucasta, Going to the Wars
questions.explanation: Lovelace wrote this celebrated lyric while detained in the Gatehouse Prison at Westminster in 1642.

questions.question: Which witty Cavalier poet and courtier is credited with inventing the card game Cribbage and wrote the song 'Why so pale and wan, fond lover?'
questions.explanation: Sir John Suckling was a wealthy courtier, playwright of Aglaura, and inventor of the card game Cribbage.

questions.question: Which seminal political treatise published in 1651 by Thomas Hobbes argued that life in the state of nature is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short?
questions.explanation: Hobbes's Leviathan advocates a social contract surrendering rights to an absolute sovereign to prevent anarchy.

questions.question: Which remarkable spiritual autobiography and confession of faith was composed in 1635 by the physician Sir Thomas Browne?
questions.explanation: Religio Medici explores the religious beliefs and tolerant scientific curiosity of a practicing doctor.

questions.question: What is the title of John Milton's 1637 pastoral elegy commemorating the tragic drowning of his Cambridge friend Edward King in the Irish Sea?
questions.explanation: Milton's Lycidas mourns his fellow poet while delivering a fierce indictment of the corrupt English clergy.

questions.question: Which 1634 courtly dramatic masque was composed by John Milton and staged at Ludlow Castle to celebrate the Earl of Bridgewater?
options: Comus (A Maske Presented at Ludlow Castle)
The Vision of the Twelve Goddesses
questions.explanation: Milton's masque depicts the Lady using temperance and virtue to withstand the sensual sorceries of Comus.

questions.question: Which Elizabethan courtier, poet, and explorer wrote 'The Discovery of Guiana' and composed the epic 'History of the World' while in the Tower?
questions.explanation: Sir Walter Raleigh was a versatile courtier and adventurer, imprisoned by James I and beheaded in 1618.

questions.question: Which Elizabethan theologian authored the monumental treatise 'Of the Lawes of Ecclesiasticall Politie' defending the Anglican Church?
questions.explanation: Richard Hooker provided the theological and philosophical defense of the Anglican Via Media against Puritanism.

questions.question: Who compiled the monumental Elizabethan travel compendium 'The Principal Navigations, Voiages, Traffiques and Discoueries of the English Nation' (1589)?
questions.explanation: Richard Hakluyt's accounts of global sea voyages promoted English exploration, trade, and colonisation.

questions.question: Which 1553 work by schoolmaster Nicholas Udall is universally recognized as the earliest surviving regular comedy written in the English language?
questions.explanation: Nicholas Udall adapted Plautus's Braggart Soldier to create the first five-act English comedy.

questions.question: Which 1561 academic drama by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville is celebrated as the earliest regular tragedy in blank verse in English?
questions.explanation: Gorboduc adapted Senecan tragedy and unrhymed blank verse to warn against political disunity.

questions.question: What broad philosophical cultural movement, rooted in the recovery of Greek and Roman classical learning, sparked the Renaissance in Europe?
questions.explanation: Renaissance Humanism celebrated human dignity, secular learning, classical rhetoric, and scientific enquiry.

questions.question: The catastrophic defeat of which naval invasion fleet in July 1588 unified England and sparked a surge of patriotic Elizabethan literature?
questions.explanation: The defeat of King Philip II's Armada secured Protestant England and fueled patriotic confidence.
